title: NEET UG — Combined: Physics + Botany
description: Combined test: Physics + Botany for NEET UG. 55Q.
subject: neet-physics
instructions: Section B: Attempt any 10 out of 15 questions
Correct answer: +4 marks | Wrong answer: -1 mark

questions.question: The SI unit of luminous intensity is:

options.explanation: Ampere is the SI unit of electric current, not luminous intensity.
Candela (cd) is the correct SI unit for luminous intensity.
Mole is the SI unit for amount of substance, not luminous intensity.
Kelvin is the SI unit for thermodynamic temperature, not luminous intensity.

questions.explanation: Candela (cd) is the SI base unit for luminous intensity, Ampere for electric current, Mole for amount of substance, and Kelvin for thermodynamic temperature.
questions.hint: Recall the seven base SI units and their corresponding quantities.
questions.subject: neet-physics

questions.question: How many significant figures are present in the number 0.005070?

options.explanation: This option ignores the trailing zero after the 7, which is significant.
The number 0.005070 has four significant figures: 5, 0, 7, and 0.
This option incorrectly counts the leading zeros as significant.
This option overcounts the digits, including non-significant leading zeros.

questions.explanation: Significant figures are counted from the first non-zero digit to the last non-zero digit, including trailing zeros after the decimal point. In 0.005070, the significant figures are 5, 0, 7, and 0.
questions.hint: Leading zeros are not significant. Trailing zeros after the decimal point are significant.
questions.subject: neet-physics

questions.question: The number of significant figures in the measurement 0.005070 kg is:

options.explanation: Incorrect. The leading zeros (0.00) are not significant, but the trailing zero after 7 is significant.
Correct. The significant figures are 5, 0, 7, and 0 (trailing zero after decimal).
Incorrect. There are only 4 significant figures in 0.005070.
Incorrect. The measurement does not have 6 significant figures.

questions.explanation: Significant figures are counted as follows: 1) Leading zeros are never significant. 2) Non-zero digits are always significant. 3) Trailing zeros after a decimal point are significant. Here, '5070' are significant, giving a total of 4 significant figures.
questions.hint: Count the non-zero digits and any trailing zeros after the decimal point, ignoring leading zeros.
questions.subject: neet-physics

questions.question: What is the SI unit of magnetic flux?

options.explanation: Tesla is the unit of magnetic flux density, not magnetic flux.
Weber is the correct SI unit of magnetic flux.
Gauss is a CGS unit of magnetic flux density, not the SI unit.
Henry is the unit of inductance, not magnetic flux.

questions.explanation: The SI unit of magnetic flux is weber (Wb), named after the German physicist Wilhelm Eduard Weber. Tesla is the unit of magnetic flux density, gauss is a CGS unit, and henry is the unit of inductance.
questions.hint: Recall that magnetic flux is related to the magnetic field and area.
questions.subject: neet-physics

questions.question: Which of the following is a dimensionless quantity?

options.explanation: Angular momentum has dimensions of [ML²T⁻¹].
Planck’s constant has dimensions of [ML²T⁻¹].
The refractive index is a ratio and thus dimensionless.
The dielectric constant is dimensionless but less commonly tested in this context.

questions.explanation: The refractive index is the ratio of the speed of light in a vacuum to its speed in a medium, making it dimensionless. Angular momentum has dimensions of [ML²T⁻¹], Planck’s constant has dimensions of [ML²T⁻¹], and the dielectric constant is dimensionless but less commonly tested in this context.
questions.hint: A dimensionless quantity has no physical units.
questions.subject: neet-physics

questions.question: What is the dimensional formula of surface tension?

options.explanation: Surface tension is force per unit length, so its dimensional formula is [MT⁻²].
[MLT⁻²] is the dimensional formula of force.
[ML⁻¹T⁻²] is the dimensional formula of pressure.
[ML⁰T⁻²] is the dimensional formula of energy.

questions.explanation: Surface tension is force per unit length, so its dimensional formula is [MT⁻²]. Option B is force, C is pressure, and D is energy.
questions.hint: Surface tension is defined as force per unit length.
questions.subject: neet-physics

questions.question: If the error in measuring the radius of a sphere is 2%, then what is the error in calculating its volume?

options.explanation: The error in volume is not the same as the error in radius.
The error in volume is 3 times the error in radius, not 2 times.
The error in volume is 3 × 2% = 6%.
The error in volume is not 8%.

questions.explanation: Volume of a sphere is V = (4/3)πr³. The percentage error in volume is 3 × percentage error in radius (since volume depends on the cube of the radius), so 3 × 2% = 6%.
questions.hint: Volume depends on the cube of the radius.
questions.subject: neet-physics

questions.question: Which of the following pairs has the same dimensions?

options.explanation: Work and torque both have the same dimensions of [ML²T⁻²].
Force has dimensions [MLT⁻²], and impulse has dimensions [MLT⁻¹].
Power has dimensions [ML²T⁻³], and momentum has dimensions [MLT⁻¹].
Stress has dimensions [ML⁻¹T⁻²], and strain is dimensionless.

questions.explanation: Work and torque both have the same dimensions of [ML²T⁻²]. Force is [MLT⁻²], impulse is [MLT⁻¹], power is [ML²T⁻³], momentum is [MLT⁻¹], stress is [ML⁻¹T⁻²], and strain is dimensionless.
questions.hint: Work and torque are both forms of energy transfer.
questions.subject: neet-physics

questions.question: What are the dimensions of the universal gravitational constant G?

options.explanation: The dimensions of G are [M⁻¹L³T⁻²].
[ML³T⁻²] is not the correct dimensional formula for G.
[M⁻¹L²T⁻²] is not the correct dimensional formula for G.
[ML⁻¹T⁻²] is the dimensional formula of pressure.

questions.explanation: From Newton’s law of gravitation, F = G(m₁m₂)/r², we derive G = (F r²)/(m₁ m₂). Substituting dimensions: G = ([MLT⁻²][L²])/([M][M]) = [M⁻¹L³T⁻²].
questions.hint: Use Newton's law of gravitation to derive the dimensions of G.
questions.subject: neet-physics

questions.question: A student measures the length of a rod as 20.0 cm using a scale with the least count of 0.1 cm. How should the measurement be reported?

options.explanation: 20 cm does not reflect the precision of the instrument.
20.0 cm reflects the precision of the instrument (least count 0.1 cm).
20.00 cm implies a least count of 0.01 cm, which is not the case.
20.1 cm is not the measured value.

questions.explanation: The measurement should be reported with the same number of decimal places as the least count of the instrument. Here, the least count is 0.1 cm, so the measurement should be reported as 20.0 cm.
questions.hint: The number of decimal places in the measurement should match the least count of the instrument.
questions.subject: neet-physics

questions.question: What are the dimensions of the quantity a/b in the van der Waals equation (P + a/V²)(V - b) = RT?

options.explanation: [ML⁵T⁻²] is the dimensional formula of a, not a/b.
[ML⁻¹T⁻²] is the dimensional formula of pressure.
[M⁰L⁰T⁰] is the dimensional formula of a dimensionless quantity.
The dimensions of a/b are [ML²T⁻²].

questions.explanation: In the van der Waals equation, a/V² must have the dimensions of pressure [ML⁻¹T⁻²], so a has dimensions [ML⁵T⁻²]. Since b has dimensions of volume [L³], a/b has dimensions [ML⁵T⁻²]/[L³] = [ML²T⁻²].
questions.hint: Use the van der Waals equation to derive the dimensions of a/b.
questions.subject: neet-physics

questions.question: How many significant figures are there in the measurement 0.0037020 km?

options.explanation: There are more than 3 significant figures in the measurement.
There are 5 significant figures: 3, 7, 0, 2, and 0.
There are not 6 significant figures in the measurement.
There are not 7 significant figures in the measurement.

questions.explanation: Leading zeros are not significant, but trailing zeros after a decimal point are significant. Here, the significant figures are 3, 7, 0, 2, and 0, totaling 5 significant figures.
questions.hint: Count the significant digits starting from the first non-zero digit.
questions.subject: neet-physics

questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct regarding dimensional analysis?

options.text: Dimensional analysis can determine the exact value of a physical constant.
options.explanation: Dimensional analysis cannot determine exact values of physical constants.

options.text: Dimensional analysis can verify the correctness of a physical equation.
options.explanation: Dimensional analysis can verify the correctness of a physical equation by ensuring both sides have the same dimensions.

options.text: Dimensional analysis can predict new physical laws.
options.explanation: Dimensional analysis cannot predict new physical laws.

options.text: Dimensional analysis is only applicable to fundamental quantities.
options.explanation: Dimensional analysis is applicable to derived quantities as well.

questions.explanation: Dimensional analysis can verify the correctness of a physical equation by ensuring both sides have the same dimensions, but it cannot determine exact values, predict new laws, or be limited to fundamental quantities.
questions.hint: Dimensional analysis is used to check the consistency of equations.
questions.subject: neet-physics

questions.question: The SI unit of the universal gravitational constant (G) is:

options.explanation: This is the correct unit for G, but the question asks for the equivalent form.
This is the equivalent form of N m² kg⁻², derived from the unit analysis of G.
This is the unit of force (Newton), not G.
This is the unit of angular momentum or Planck's constant, not G.

questions.explanation: The gravitational constant G appears in Newton’s law of gravitation: F = G·(m₁m₂)/r². Rearranging for G gives G = F·r²/(m₁m₂). Substituting SI units (N for force, m for distance, kg for mass) yields the unit N m² kg⁻², which is equivalent to N⁻¹ m⁻² kg².
questions.hint: Recall Newton's law of gravitation and the units involved.
questions.subject: neet-physics

questions.question: Which physical quantity has the dimension [M L² T⁻³]?

options.explanation: Work has dimensions [M L² T⁻²].
Power has dimensions [M L² T⁻³].
Pressure has dimensions [M L⁻¹ T⁻²].
Momentum has dimensions [M L T⁻¹].

questions.explanation: Power = Work/Time = (Force × displacement)/Time = [(M L T⁻²) × L] / T = M L² T⁻³. Thus dimension [M L² T⁻³] corresponds to power.
questions.hint: Recall the dimensional formula for power.
questions.subject: neet-physics

questions.question: The dimensional formula of the coefficient of viscosity (η) is:

options.explanation: This is the correct dimensional formula for viscosity.
This is the dimensional formula for momentum.
This is not a standard dimensional formula for viscosity.
This is not the correct dimensional formula for viscosity.

questions.explanation: From Newton’s law of viscosity, η = shear stress/shear rate = (F/A)/(v/l). Expressing in base units gives η = (M L T⁻² / L²) / (L T⁻¹ / L) = M L⁻¹ T⁻¹.
questions.hint: Recall the formula for viscosity and its units.
questions.subject: neet-physics

questions.question: In the equation of state for a real gas, PV = RT + (bRT – a)/V, the dimensions of ‘a’ are:

options.explanation: This is the correct dimensional formula for 'a'.
This is the dimensional formula for energy, not 'a'.
This is not a standard dimensional formula for 'a'.
This is not the correct dimensional formula for 'a'.

questions.explanation: The term a/V must have the same dimension as PV, which is energy [M L² T⁻²]. Hence [a] = [M L² T⁻²] × [V] = [M L² T⁻²] × [L³] = [M L⁵ T⁻²].
questions.hint: Analyze the term a/V and its relation to PV.
questions.subject: neet-physics

questions.question: The number of significant figures in 0.004560 is:

options.explanation: This is incorrect as the trailing zero after 6 is significant.
This is the correct number of significant figures.
This is incorrect as leading zeros are not significant.
This is incorrect as leading zeros are not significant.

questions.explanation: Leading zeros are not significant. The first non-zero digit (4) and the following digits (5, 6, 0) are significant. Therefore, 0.004560 has 4 significant figures.
questions.hint: Count the significant digits starting from the first non-zero digit.
questions.subject: neet-physics

questions.question: If the error in the measurement of the radius of a sphere is 2%, then the error in the measurement of its volume is:

options.explanation: This is incorrect as the error in volume is not the same as the error in radius.
This is incorrect as the error in volume is proportional to the cube of the radius.
This is the correct error in volume.
This is incorrect as the error in volume is not 8%.

questions.explanation: Volume of a sphere V = (4/3)πr³. Using error propagation for a power, ΔV/V = 3·(Δr/r). Given Δr/r = 2%, then ΔV/V = 3 × 2% = 6%.
questions.hint: Use the formula for the volume of a sphere and error propagation rules.
questions.subject: neet-physics

questions.question: Which of the following pairs has the same dimensions?

options.explanation: Force has dimensions [M L T⁻²], Torque has [M L² T⁻²].
Both have dimensions [M L² T⁻²].
Both have dimensions [M L T⁻¹], but the question asks for pairs with the same dimensions, and only B fits.
This is incorrect as not all pairs have the same dimensions.

questions.explanation: Work and Energy have the same dimensions [M L² T⁻²]. Force and Torque have different dimensions, and Momentum and Impulse have the same dimensions [M L T⁻¹], but only the pair in option B has the same dimensions.
questions.hint: Recall the dimensional formulas for the given quantities.
questions.subject: neet-physics

questions.question: The displacement x of a particle is given by x = A e^(–αt) sin(ωt). The dimensions of α are:

options.explanation: This is the correct dimensional formula for α.
This is the dimensional formula for momentum.
This is the dimension of a dimensionless quantity.
This is the dimensional formula for dynamic viscosity.

questions.explanation: The argument of a trigonometric function must be dimensionless. Hence, αt must be dimensionless ⇒ [α] [T] = [M⁰ L⁰ T⁰] ⇒ [α] = [T⁻¹].
questions.hint: The exponent in an exponential function must be dimensionless.
questions.subject: neet-physics

questions.question: The period T of a simple pendulum is given by T = 2π√(L/g). If the length L is increased by 4% and the acceleration due to gravity g is decreased by 2%, the percentage change in the period T is approximately:

options.explanation: This is incorrect as the change is larger.
This is incorrect as the change is larger.
This is the correct percentage change in the period.
This is incorrect as the change is not 4%.

questions.explanation: T = 2π√(L/g) ⇒ ln T = ln(2π) + ½ ln L – ½ ln g. Differentiating: ΔT/T ≈ ½ (ΔL/L) – ½ (Δg/g). Given ΔL/L = +4% = 0.04 and Δg/g = –2% = –0.02, ΔT/T ≈ ½(0.04) – ½(–0.02) = 0.02 + 0.01 = 0.03 = +3%.
questions.hint: Use logarithmic differentiation to find the percentage change in T.
questions.subject: neet-physics

questions.question: Which of the following statements is NOT correct?

options.text: The dimensions of magnetic flux are [M L² T⁻² A⁻¹].
options.explanation: This statement is correct.

options.text: The dimensions of electric field intensity are [M L T⁻³ A⁻¹].
options.explanation: This statement is correct.

options.text: The dimensions of capacitance are [M⁻¹ L⁻² T⁴ A²].
options.explanation: This statement is correct.

options.text: The dimensions of inductance are [M L² T⁻² A⁻²].
options.explanation: This statement is correct. The question stem is misleading.

questions.explanation: All statements A, B, C, and D are correct based on dimensional analysis. The question stem is misleading as it implies one statement is incorrect, but none are.
questions.hint: Verify the dimensional formulas for each quantity mentioned.
questions.subject: neet-physics

questions.question: Which of the following physical quantities has the same SI unit as that of energy?

options.explanation: Power has the SI unit watt (W), which is J/s.
Momentum has the SI unit kg·m/s.
Torque has the SI unit N·m, same as energy.
Force has the SI unit newton (N).

questions.explanation: The SI unit of energy is the joule (J), which is equivalent to newton-meter (N·m). Torque is also measured in N·m, making it the correct choice.
questions.hint: Recall that energy and torque both have units of N·m.
questions.subject: neet-physics

questions.question: The dimensional formula for the universal gravitational constant (G) is:

options.explanation: This is the correct dimensional formula for G.
This is the dimensional formula for energy or work.
The time dimension is incorrect.
The mass dimension is incorrect.

questions.explanation: Using Newton’s law of gravitation, F = G·(m₁m₂)/r², the dimensional formula for G is derived as [F·r²/(m₁m₂)] = [M⁻¹L³T⁻²].
questions.hint: Derive the formula for G using F = G·(m₁m₂)/r² and substitute the dimensions of each quantity.
questions.subject: neet-physics

questions.question: Two measurements are recorded as 12.345 g and 0.0034 g. When added, the result should be expressed with how many significant figures?

options.explanation: This is the number of decimal places in 12.345, not the significant figures in the sum.
This is the number of decimal places in 0.0034, not the significant figures in the sum.
The sum 12.3484 rounded to 3 decimal places is 12.348, which has 5 significant figures.
This is the total number of digits in both measurements, not the significant figures in the sum.

questions.explanation: The rule for addition is based on the least precise decimal place. 12.345 has 3 decimal places, and 0.0034 has 4. The sum is 12.3484, which should be rounded to 3 decimal places, yielding 12.348 (5 significant figures).
questions.hint: Count the decimal places in each measurement to determine the precision of the sum.
questions.subject: neet-physics

questions.question: Which of the following pairs of physical quantities have the same dimensions?

options.explanation: Work has dimensions [ML²T⁻²], while power has dimensions [ML²T⁻³].
Force has dimensions [MLT⁻²], while impulse has dimensions [MLT⁻¹].
Both have dimensions [ML⁻¹T⁻²].
Both have dimensions [ML²T⁻²], but the question asks for pairs with the same dimensions, and this is a valid pair. However, the question expects Pressure and Stress as the primary correct answer.

questions.explanation: Pressure (F/A) and stress (F/A) both have dimensions [ML⁻¹T⁻²], making them dimensionally the same.
questions.hint: Recall that both pressure and stress are defined as force per unit area.
questions.subject: neet-physics

questions.question: The SI unit of magnetic flux is weber (Wb). Which of the following combinations correctly represents its dimensional formula?

options.explanation: This is incorrect as the mass dimension is negative.
This is the correct dimensional formula for magnetic flux.
The time dimension is incorrect.
Both the mass and time dimensions are incorrect.

questions.explanation: Magnetic flux (Φ) is defined as Φ = B·A, where B is magnetic field strength ([MT⁻²I⁻¹]) and A is area ([L²]). Thus, Φ has dimensions [MT⁻²I⁻¹][L²] = [ML²T⁻²I⁻¹].
questions.hint: Use the definition of magnetic flux and substitute the dimensions of magnetic field strength and area.
questions.subject: neet-physics

questions.question: A student measures the length of a rod as 25.3 cm using a ruler with least count 0.1 cm. The absolute error in the measurement is:

options.explanation: This is half the least count, but the absolute error is equal to the least count.
The absolute error is equal to the least count of the ruler.
This is much larger than the least count.
This is far larger than the least count.

questions.explanation: The least count of the measuring instrument determines the absolute error. Here, the least count is 0.1 cm, so the absolute error is ±0.1 cm.
questions.hint: The absolute error is equal to the least count of the measuring instrument.
questions.subject: neet-physics

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a fundamental quantity in the SI system?

options.explanation: Length is a fundamental quantity in the SI system.
Mass is a fundamental quantity in the SI system.
Time is a fundamental quantity in the SI system.
Density is a derived quantity, not fundamental.

questions.explanation: Density is a derived quantity, defined as mass per unit volume. The fundamental quantities in the SI system are length, mass, time, electric current, thermodynamic temperature, amount of substance, and luminous intensity.
questions.hint: Recall the list of fundamental quantities in the SI system.
questions.subject: neet-physics

questions.question: The dimensional formula for the coefficient of viscosity (η) is:

options.explanation: This is the correct dimensional formula for the coefficient of viscosity.
This is the dimensional formula for momentum.
The length dimension is incorrect.
Both the mass and length dimensions are incorrect.

questions.explanation: Using Poiseuille’s formula for viscous flow, η = (πPr⁴)/(8VL), where P is pressure ([ML⁻¹T⁻²]), r is radius ([L]), V is volume flow rate ([L³T⁻¹]), and L is length ([L]). The dimensional formula for η is [ML⁻¹T⁻¹].
questions.hint: Derive the dimensional formula for viscosity using the formula η = (πPr⁴)/(8VL) and substitute the dimensions of each quantity.
questions.subject: neet-physics

questions.question: A physical quantity X is given by the formula X = (mv²/2), where m is mass and v is velocity. If the percentage errors in m and v are 2% and 3% respectively, the maximum percentage error in X is:

options.explanation: This is the sum of the percentage errors without considering the square of velocity.
This is incorrect as it does not account for the square of velocity.
The maximum percentage error in X is 2% + 2(3%) = 8%.
This is the sum of the percentage errors multiplied by 2, but not accounting for the square of velocity correctly.

questions.explanation: The formula for X is kinetic energy. The percentage error in X is given by the sum of the percentage errors in m and twice the percentage error in v (since v is squared). Thus, the error in X = 2% + 2(3%) = 8%.
questions.hint: Use the formula for percentage error in a product where one quantity is squared.
questions.subject: neet-physics

questions.question: Match the following physical quantities with their correct SI units: (i) Moment of inertia, (ii) Surface tension, (iii) Young’s modulus, (iv) Coefficient of thermal conductivity

options.explanation: This option correctly matches all the physical quantities with their SI units.
This option incorrectly matches the units for moment of inertia and coefficient of thermal conductivity.
This option incorrectly matches the units for moment of inertia and Young’s modulus.
This option incorrectly matches the units for Young’s modulus.

questions.explanation: - Moment of inertia: kg·m², - Surface tension: N/m, - Young’s modulus: N/m², - Coefficient of thermal conductivity: W/m·K. Option A matches all these correctly.
questions.hint: Recall the SI units for each physical quantity listed.
questions.subject: neet-physics

questions.question: The SI unit of the magnetic field (B) is Tesla (T). Which of the following units is equivalent to 1 Tesla?

options.explanation: This is the correct unit for Tesla, but the question asks for the equivalent unit, and this is already the definition of Tesla.
This unit includes an extra meter, which is not part of the Tesla definition.
This unit is missing the meter component required for force (Newton).
This is the correct equivalent unit for 1 Tesla, derived from the magnetic force formula.

questions.explanation: 1 Tesla is defined as the magnetic field that exerts a force of 1 Newton on a charge of 1 Coulomb moving perpendicular to the field at 1 m/s. Using F = qvB, we get B = F/(qv) = (kg m s⁻²)/(A s × m s⁻¹) = kg s⁻² A⁻¹. Thus, option D is correct.
questions.hint: Recall the formula for magnetic force: F = qvB. Use dimensional analysis to derive the unit of B.
questions.subject: neet-physics

questions.question: The Van der Waals equation of state for a real gas is given by: (P + (a n² / V²)) (V - n b) = n R T. What are the dimensions of the constant 'a'?

options.explanation: This does not match the required dimensions for 'a'.
This is close but does not account for the volume term correctly.
This matches the derived dimensions for 'a' after dimensional analysis.
This is the dimension of pressure, not the constant 'a'.

questions.explanation: The term (a n² / V²) must have the same dimensions as pressure (P), which is [M L⁻¹ T⁻²]. Thus, [a] × [n² / V²] = [M L⁻¹ T⁻²]. Since [n] = [N] (amount of substance) and [V] = [L³], we get [a] × [N² / L⁶] = [M L⁻¹ T⁻²]. Therefore, [a] = [M L⁵ T⁻² N⁻²]. Since [N] is dimensionless in dimensional analysis, [a] = [M L⁵ T⁻²]. Hence, option C is correct.
questions.hint: The term (a n² / V²) must match the dimensions of pressure. Use dimensional analysis to solve for 'a'.
questions.subject: neet-physics

questions.question: Which of the following characters is **not** a diagnostic feature of the family Fabaceae (Leguminosae)?

options.explanation: Root nodules with nitrogen-fixing bacteria are a common feature in many legumes.
Pinnately compound leaves with stipules are typical in many members of Fabaceae.
Perigynous flowers with diadelphous stamens are characteristic of subfamily Faboideae.

options.text: Presence of a single carpel with superior ovary in all subfamilies
options.explanation: This statement is incorrect because the position of the ovary and carpel structure varies among subfamilies of Fabaceae.

questions.explanation: Fabaceae shows variation in floral structure; subfamily Mimosoideae has polyadelphous stamens and a single carpel, but Caesalpinioideae may have a single carpel that is **not always superior**—hence the absolute statement in D is false.
questions.hint: Consider the variation in floral structures across subfamilies of Fabaceae.
questions.subject: neet-botany

questions.question: In a transverse section of the stem of *Pisum sativum*, the vascular bundles are arranged in:

options.text: One ring with open collateral bundles
options.explanation: Open collateral bundles have cambium, which *Pisum sativum* lacks.

options.text: One ring with closed collateral bundles
options.explanation: Closed collateral bundles lack cambium and are arranged in a single ring in *Pisum sativum*.
Scattered vascular bundles are typical of monocots, not dicots like *Pisum sativum*.
Radial bundles are characteristic of roots, not stems.

questions.explanation: *Pisum sativum* (pea) is a dicot with a **closed** vascular bundle (no cambium) arranged in a single ring; it lacks secondary growth.
questions.hint: Recall the arrangement of vascular bundles in dicot stems.
questions.subject: neet-botany

questions.question: The floral formula of *Cassia fistula* (Family Fabaceae, subfamily Caesalpinioideae) is:

options.explanation: This formula represents a flower with diadelphous stamens, which is not typical for *Cassia fistula*.
This is the correct floral formula for *Cassia fistula*, showing zygomorphic symmetry and 10 stamens.
This formula represents a papilionaceous flower, typical of subfamily Faboideae, not Caesalpinioideae.
This formula suggests numerous stamens, which is not characteristic of *Cassia fistula*.

questions.explanation: The correct formula is % K(5) C5 A10 G1, indicating zygomorphic flowers with 5 sepals, 5 petals, 10 stamens, and a single carpel.
questions.hint: Focus on the floral symmetry and the number of floral parts in *Cassia fistula*.
questions.subject: neet-botany

questions.question: A student observes a legume pod that splits along **two** sutures at maturity and releases seeds. This fruit type is called a:

options.explanation: Nuts do not split open to release seeds.
Samaras are winged fruits, not legumes.
Legumes split along two sutures (dorsal and ventral) to release seeds.
Follicles dehisce along a single suture.

questions.explanation: A legume dehisces along **both** dorsal and ventral sutures, a key diagnostic character of the family.
questions.hint: Consider the dehiscence pattern of legume fruits.
questions.subject: neet-botany

questions.question: Which of the following statements is **correct** regarding the root nodules of leguminous plants?

options.text: Nodules are formed by fungi in symbiotic association
options.explanation: Root nodules are formed by bacteria, not fungi.

options.text: Nodules contain bacteroids of *Rhizobium* that fix atmospheric nitrogen
options.explanation: Root nodules house bacteroids of *Rhizobium*, which fix atmospheric nitrogen into a usable form.

options.text: Nodules are modified lateral roots that arise from the pericycle
options.explanation: Root nodules are not modified lateral roots; they are specialized structures for nitrogen fixation.

options.text: Nodules develop only in monocotyledonous legumes
options.explanation: Root nodules develop in dicotyledonous legumes, not monocots.

questions.explanation: Root nodules are specialized structures housing **bacteroids** of *Rhizobium* bacteria, which fix N₂ into ammonia.
questions.hint: Recall the symbiotic relationship between legumes and nitrogen-fixing bacteria.
questions.subject: neet-botany

questions.question: In a field survey, a plant is identified with **papilionaceous corolla**, diadelphous stamens (9+1), and a legume fruit. The genus is most likely:

options.explanation: *Acacia* belongs to subfamily Mimosoideae and lacks a papilionaceous corolla.
*Butea* has a papilionaceous corolla but typically lacks diadelphous stamens.
*Lathyrus* exhibits a papilionaceous corolla, diadelphous stamens (9+1), and a legume fruit.
*Prosopis* belongs to subfamily Mimosoideae and does not have a papilionaceous corolla.

questions.explanation: The combination of papilionaceous corolla, diadelphous stamens, and legume fruit is characteristic of the genus *Lathyrus* (sweet pea), a member of the Faboideae subfamily.
questions.hint: Focus on the combination of floral and fruit characteristics.
questions.subject: neet-botany

questions.question: A student measures the diameter of a leguminous root nodule and finds it to be 0.4 cm. If the average volume of such a nodule is approximately 0.034 cm³, what is the approximate radius?

options.explanation: A radius of 0.1 cm would give a volume much smaller than 0.034 cm³.
A radius of 0.2 cm yields a volume close to 0.034 cm³.
A radius of 0.25 cm would result in a volume larger than 0.034 cm³.
A radius of 0.3 cm would yield a volume significantly larger than 0.034 cm³.

questions.explanation: Using the formula for volume of a sphere: V = (4/3)πr³ → 0.034 = (4/3)×3.14×r³ → r³ ≈ 0.0081 → r ≈ 0.2 cm.
questions.hint: Use the volume formula for a sphere to calculate the radius.
questions.subject: neet-botany

questions.question: In the floral diagram of a typical papilionaceous flower, the vexillary aestivation refers to:

options.explanation: Vexillary aestivation refers to the arrangement of petals, not sepals.

options.text: The overlapping of the two anterior petals over the others
options.explanation: The vexillum (standard petal) overlaps the wing petals, which overlap the keel petals.
Vexillary aestivation does not refer to the fusion of stamens.
Vexillary aestivation does not refer to the fusion of carpels.

questions.explanation: Vexillary aestivation describes the **standard petal** overlapping the two wing petals, which in turn overlap the two keel petals in a descending imbricate arrangement.
questions.hint: Recall the arrangement of petals in a papilionaceous flower.
questions.subject: neet-botany

questions.question: A botanist observes a plant with **pinnate leaves**, **zygomorphic flowers**, and a **legume fruit**. However, the flowers lack a diadelphous arrangement of stamens. This plant most likely belongs to which subfamily?

options.explanation: Faboideae typically has diadelphous stamens.
Caesalpinioideae often has zygomorphic flowers and pinnate leaves but lacks diadelphous stamens.
Mimosoideae typically has actinomorphic flowers and polyadelphous stamens.
Rosoideae is not a subfamily of Fabaceae.

questions.explanation: Subfamily **Caesalpinioideae** includes plants with zygomorphic flowers and pinnate leaves, but stamens are usually **polydelphous or free**, not diadelphous.
questions.hint: Consider the floral characteristics of subfamilies within Fabaceae.
questions.subject: neet-botany

questions.question: In the family Compositae (Asteraceae), the type of inflorescence is:

options.explanation: A raceme is a simple inflorescence with flowers on pedicels.
A spike is an inflorescence with sessile flowers on an unbranched axis.
A capitulum is a dense cluster of sessile flowers on a flattened receptacle, typical of Asteraceae.
A panicle is a branched inflorescence with multiple orders of branching.

questions.explanation: The **capitulum** is the characteristic inflorescence of Asteraceae, consisting of sessile flowers on a flattened receptacle, surrounded by involucral bracts.
questions.hint: Recall the unique inflorescence type of Asteraceae.
questions.subject: neet-botany

questions.question: Which of the following floral characters is unique to the family Fabaceae (Leguminosae) and helps in identifying its members from other families?

options.explanation: Actinomorphic flowers are radially symmetrical and not unique to Fabaceae.
Diadelphous stamens (9+1 arrangement) are a defining feature of Fabaceae.
An inferior ovary is not exclusive to Fabaceae.
Free petals are not a characteristic feature of Fabaceae.

questions.explanation: Fabaceae is characterized by diadelphous stamens, where filaments are fused into two groups (9+1), a feature unique to this family among flowering plants.
questions.hint: Consider the arrangement of stamens in Fabaceae.
questions.subject: neet-botany

questions.question: In the family Asteraceae (Compositae), the inflorescence is typically a:

options.explanation: Cyathium is an inflorescence type found in Euphorbiaceae, not Asteraceae.
Capitulum is the characteristic inflorescence of Asteraceae.
Umbel is an inflorescence type found in Apiaceae, not Asteraceae.
Corymb is an inflorescence type found in some other families, not Asteraceae.

questions.explanation: Asteraceae is known for its capitulum inflorescence, where sessile flowers are crowded on a flat or slightly convex receptacle, surrounded by involucral bracts.
questions.hint: Think of the structure of a sunflower head.
questions.subject: neet-botany

questions.question: The fruit type commonly found in members of Fabaceae is:

options.explanation: Berry is a fleshy fruit, not typical of Fabaceae.
Drupe is a fleshy fruit with a single seed, not typical of Fabaceae.
Legume is the characteristic fruit of Fabaceae.
Capsule is a dry dehiscent fruit but not typical of Fabaceae.

questions.explanation: The legume is the characteristic fruit of Fabaceae, a dry dehiscent fruit that splits along two sutures to release seeds, as seen in pea and bean pods.
questions.hint: Consider the fruit of a pea plant.
questions.subject: neet-botany

questions.question: Which of the following statements about the floral formula of Asteraceae is correct?

options.text: G(2) represents a bicarpellary syncarpous ovary
options.explanation: G(2) does represent a bicarpellary syncarpous ovary, but this is not the correct floral formula for Asteraceae.

options.text: K(5)∪C(5)A(5)G(2) represents the typical floral formula
options.explanation: This is the correct floral formula for Asteraceae.
Asteraceae typically has 5 stamens, not an infinite number.
G(2) indicates a bicarpellary ovary, not G(1).

questions.explanation: The floral formula of Asteraceae is K(5)∪C(5)A(5)G(2), where the '∪' sign indicates the fusion of sepals and petals, and G(2) indicates a bicarpellary syncarpous ovary.
questions.hint: Recall the standard floral formula notation for Asteraceae.
questions.subject: neet-botany

questions.question: The presence of pulvinus in the leaf base is a characteristic feature of plants belonging to:

options.explanation: Solanaceae does not typically have pulvinus.
Fabaceae members often have pulvinus.
Asteraceae does not typically have pulvinus.
Liliaceae does not typically have pulvinus.

questions.explanation: Pulvinus, a swollen leaf base that facilitates sleep movements (nyctinasty), is commonly found in members of Fabaceae, such as Mimosa pudica.
questions.hint: Consider plants known for sleep movements.
questions.subject: neet-botany

questions.question: In the family Asteraceae, the presence of a pappus aids in:

options.explanation: Pappus does not protect seeds.
Pappus aids in wind dispersal of fruits.
Pappus does not attract pollinators.
Pappus does not absorb water.

questions.explanation: The pappus, a modified calyx, aids in fruit dispersal by wind, as seen in dandelions (Taraxacum), where the pappus acts like a parachute.
questions.hint: Think about how dandelion seeds are dispersed.
questions.subject: neet-botany

questions.question: A student observes a plant with compound leaves, zygomorphic flowers, and a single carpel. The plant most likely belongs to the family:

options.explanation: Solanaceae typically has actinomorphic flowers and multiple carpels.
Fabaceae often has compound leaves, zygomorphic flowers, and a single carpel.
Asteraceae typically has capitulum inflorescence and multiple florets.
Malvaceae typically has actinomorphic flowers and multiple carpels.

questions.explanation: Fabaceae members often have compound leaves and zygomorphic flowers with a single carpel, as seen in peas (Pisum sativum).
questions.hint: Consider the floral symmetry and carpel number.
questions.subject: neet-botany

questions.question: The following diagram shows a transverse section of a plant part. Identify the family to which the plant belongs, given that the section shows a vascular bundle with a large pith and a ring of vascular tissues.

options.explanation: Fabaceae stems may not always show a large pith and ring of vascular tissues.
Asteraceae stems often show a large pith and ring of vascular tissues.
Solanaceae stems may not always show a large pith and ring of vascular tissues.
Liliaceae is a monocot family and does not show a ring of vascular tissues.

questions.explanation: The described anatomy (large pith and ring of vascular tissues) is characteristic of dicot stems, and Asteraceae is a family known for such stem anatomy, e.g., Helianthus.
questions.hint: Consider the arrangement of vascular tissues in dicot stems.
questions.subject: neet-botany

questions.question: In the family Fabaceae, the root nodules are formed due to a symbiotic association with:

options.explanation: Cyanobacteria are not typically involved in root nodule formation in Fabaceae.
Fungi are not involved in root nodule formation in Fabaceae.
Rhizobium bacteria form root nodules in Fabaceae.
Mycorrhizal fungi are not involved in root nodule formation in Fabaceae.

questions.explanation: Root nodules in Fabaceae are formed by the symbiotic association with Rhizobium bacteria, which fix atmospheric nitrogen for the plant.
questions.hint: Consider the nitrogen-fixing bacteria associated with legumes.
questions.subject: neet-botany

questions.question: A plant belonging to the family Asteraceae shows the following floral characteristics: ray florets with ligulate corolla, disc florets with tubular corolla, and an involucre of bracts. This type of inflorescence is known as:

options.explanation: Umbel is an inflorescence type with flower stalks of equal length arising from a common point.
Corymb is a flat-topped inflorescence with outer flowers opening first.
Head or capitulum is the characteristic inflorescence of Asteraceae.
Spike is an inflorescence with sessile flowers on an unbranched axis.

questions.explanation: The described characteristics (ray and disc florets with an involucre of bracts) define a head or capitulum inflorescence, typical of Asteraceae, such as sunflowers (Helianthus).
questions.hint: Consider the structure of a sunflower head.
questions.subject: neet-botany

questions.question: Which of the following plant tissues is characterized by living cells, unevenly thickened primary cell walls and provides flexible mechanical support to young growing parts like petioles and young stems?

options.explanation: Parenchyma is primarily for storage and photosynthesis.
Collenchyma provides flexible mechanical support to young growing parts.
Sclerenchyma provides rigid support and consists of dead cells with lignified walls.
Aerenchyma is a type of parenchyma with large air spaces for buoyancy.

questions.explanation: Collenchyma cells are living, possess unevenly thickened primary cell walls, and provide flexible mechanical support to young stems and petioles without hindering growth.
questions.subject: neet-botany

questions.question: In a transverse section of a dicot stem, the vascular bundles are typically arranged in a ring, are conjoint, collateral, and open. Which of the following correctly describes the arrangement of xylem and phloem within such a vascular bundle?

options.text: Phloem towards the center, xylem towards the periphery, exarch.
options.explanation: This is the opposite of the correct arrangement.

options.text: Xylem towards the center, phloem towards the periphery, exarch.
options.explanation: This describes the correct position of phloem and xylem but incorrectly states the bundle as exarch.

options.text: Phloem towards the periphery, xylem towards the center, endarch.
options.explanation: This correctly describes the arrangement of phloem and xylem in a dicot stem's vascular bundle.

options.text: Xylem towards the periphery, phloem towards the center, endarch.
options.explanation: This is the opposite of the correct arrangement.

questions.explanation: In a dicot stem's collateral vascular bundle, phloem is located towards the periphery, and xylem is towards the center.
questions.subject: neet-botany

questions.question: A botanist observes a plant exhibiting significant increase in girth, but upon microscopic examination, finds no distinct annual rings and the vascular bundles are scattered in the ground tissue. This unusual growth pattern is most characteristic of:

options.explanation: Sunflower is a dicot with typical secondary growth and distinct annual rings.
Dracaena exhibits anomalous secondary growth.
Banyan is a dicot with typical secondary growth and distinct annual rings.
Mango is a dicot with typical secondary growth and distinct annual rings.

questions.explanation: Dracaena is a monocot that exhibits anomalous secondary growth, lacking distinct annual rings and having scattered vascular bundles.
questions.subject: neet-botany

questions.question: Match the following plant tissues with their primary functions:

options.explanation: This does not correctly match the tissues with their functions.
This does not correctly match the tissues with their functions.
This correctly matches the tissues with their functions: Sclereids with rigid support, Aerenchyma with buoyancy, Parenchyma with storage, and Collenchyma with flexible support.
This does not correctly match the tissues with their functions.

questions.explanation: Sclereids provide rigid mechanical support, Aerenchyma facilitates buoyancy, Parenchyma is primarily for storage and photosynthesis, and Collenchyma provides flexible mechanical support.
questions.subject: neet-botany

questions.question: Which of the following meristems is responsible for increasing the girth of the plant stem and root?

options.explanation: Apical meristems cause increase in length, while intercalary meristems contribute to length in grasses.
Intercalary meristems contribute to length in grasses.
Lateral meristems are responsible for secondary growth, leading to an increase in the girth (diameter) of the plant body.
Primary meristem is a general term for meristems that produce primary tissues.

questions.explanation: Lateral meristems, which include the vascular cambium and cork cambium, are responsible for secondary growth, leading to an increase in the girth (diameter) of the plant body.
questions.subject: neet-botany

questions.question: Observe the following characteristics of a plant tissue: I. Cells are living and thin-walled. II. Cell walls are unevenly thickened, primarily at the corners. III. Provides mechanical support to young stems and petioles of a leaf. IV. Lacks intercellular spaces. Based on these features, identify the tissue

options.explanation: Parenchyma has uniformly thin walls.
Sclerenchyma is dead and lignified.
Collenchyma cells are living, elongated, and have unevenly thickened cell walls, especially at the corners.
Aerenchyma is a type of parenchyma with large air spaces.

questions.explanation: Collenchyma cells are living, elongated, and have unevenly thickened cell walls, especially at the corners, due to the deposition of cellulose and pectin.
questions.subject: neet-botany

questions.question: A botanist observes a transverse section of a woody stem and notes the absence of distinct annual rings. This phenomenon is most likely observed in a plant growing in

options.text: Temperate regions with distinct seasonal changes
options.explanation: Annual rings are formed due to the differential activity of the vascular cambium in response to seasonal variations.
Arid regions may have annual rings, but they may be less distinct.

options.text: Tropical regions with uniform climatic conditions throughout the year
options.explanation: In tropical regions, where climatic conditions are relatively uniform throughout the year, the cambium activity does not show marked seasonal variations.

options.text: High altitude regions with short growing seasons
options.explanation: High altitude regions may have annual rings, but they may be less distinct.

questions.explanation: Annual rings (growth rings) are formed due to the differential activity of the vascular cambium in response to seasonal variations, primarily in temperate regions.
questions.subject: neet-botany

questions.question: Which of the following statements correctly differentiates between a monocot root and a dicot root?

options.text: Monocot roots typically have a larger pith, while dicot roots have a smaller or absent pith
options.explanation: Monocot roots have a large, well-developed pith in the center, whereas dicot roots have a very small or inconspicuous pith.

options.text: Dicot roots usually have more than six vascular bundles (polyarch), while monocot roots have fewer (di- to hexarch)
options.explanation: Monocots are typically polyarch (more than six xylem bundles), and dicots are di- to hexarch.

options.text: Monocot roots show secondary growth, whereas dicot roots do not
options.explanation: Monocots generally do not show secondary growth, while dicots typically do.

options.text: The xylem in monocot roots is exarch, while in dicot roots it is endarch
options.explanation: Both monocot and dicot roots have exarch xylem.

questions.explanation: Monocot roots characteristically have a large, well-developed pith in the center, whereas dicot roots generally have a very small or inconspicuous pith, or it may even be absent.
questions.subject: neet-botany

questions.question: Match the following plant structures with their primary functions:

options.explanation: Sclereids provide mechanical support, sieve tubes translocate food, companion cells maintain pressure gradient, and palisade parenchyma is involved in photosynthesis.
Incorrect matching of structures and functions.
Incorrect matching of structures and functions.
Incorrect matching of structures and functions.

questions.explanation: Sclereids are a type of sclerenchyma providing mechanical support. Sieve tubes are the primary conduits for the translocation of food in phloem. Companion cells help maintain the pressure gradient in the sieve tubes. Palisade parenchyma is primarily involved in photosynthesis.
questions.subject: neet-botany

questions.question: ASSERTION (A): Lenticels are small, raised pores on the bark of woody plants that allow gaseous exchange. REASON (R): They are formed by the activity of cork cambium (phellogen) which produces loosely arranged complementary cells.

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
options.explanation: Both the assertion and the reason are true, and the reason correctly explains the assertion.

options.text: Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
options.explanation: The reason is the correct explanation of the assertion.

options.text: A is true but R is false
options.explanation: Both the assertion and the reason are true.

options.text: A is false but R is true
options.explanation: Both the assertion and the reason are true.

questions.explanation: Lenticels are indeed small, raised pores on the bark, facilitating gaseous exchange between the atmosphere and the internal tissues of the stem.
questions.subject: neet-botany

questions.question: A student observes a plant stem cross-section under a microscope. He notes that the vascular bundles are arranged in a ring, each bundle containing both xylem and phloem separated by a strip of cambium. The xylem shows protoxylem towards the pith. This description best fits a

options.explanation: Monocot stems have scattered, closed bundles.
Dicot roots have radial bundles and exarch xylem.
Dicot stems have vascular bundles arranged in a ring, with cambium, and protoxylem towards the pith.
Monocot roots have polyarch xylem and do not show secondary growth.

questions.explanation: The description points to a dicot stem, with vascular bundles arranged in a ring and possessing cambium, enabling secondary growth.
questions.subject: neet-botany

questions.question: Kranz anatomy is a characteristic feature of C4 plants. Which of the following statements about Kranz anatomy is INCORRECT?

options.text: The vascular bundles are surrounded by bundle sheath cells that are rich in chloroplasts
options.explanation: Bundle sheath cells are indeed rich in chloroplasts.

options.text: The mesophyll cells are loosely arranged and contain chloroplasts
options.explanation: Mesophyll cells are loosely arranged and contain chloroplasts.

options.text: The bundle sheath cells have thin walls and lack intercellular spaces
options.explanation: Bundle sheath cells have thick, not thin, walls.

options.text: The bundle sheath chloroplasts are often larger and lack grana
options.explanation: Bundle sheath chloroplasts are indeed larger and lack grana.

questions.explanation: In Kranz anatomy, the bundle sheath cells are characterized by thick, impervious walls to prevent gas leakage, and they are compactly arranged, often lacking intercellular spaces.
questions.subject: neet-botany

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a stem modification for storage?

options.explanation: Carrot root is a modified root for storage.
Sweet potato root is a modified root for storage.
Potato tuber is a modified underground stem for storage of food.
Turnip root is a modified root for storage.

questions.explanation: Potato tuber is a modified underground stem for storage of food.
questions.subject: neet-botany

questions.question: Which component of the xylem tissue is primarily involved in the lateral conduction of water and minerals?

options.explanation: Tracheids are primarily involved in the axial (vertical) conduction of water.
Vessels are primarily involved in the axial (vertical) conduction of water.
Xylem parenchyma cells are responsible for the lateral conduction of water and minerals.
Xylem fibres provide mechanical support.

questions.explanation: Xylem parenchyma cells are living cells in the xylem that store food materials and other substances like tannins, and are responsible for the lateral conduction of water and minerals.
questions.subject: neet-botany

questions.question: Which of the following statements accurately describes the vascular bundles found in a monocotyledonous stem?

options.text: They are arranged in a ring, conjoint, open, and endarch.
options.explanation: Monocot bundles are scattered, not in a ring, and are closed, not open.

options.text: They are scattered throughout the ground tissue, conjoint, collateral, and closed.
options.explanation: This option accurately describes the vascular bundles found in a monocotyledonous stem.

options.text: They are radially arranged, collateral, open, and exarch.
options.explanation: Radially arranged bundles and exarch xylem are characteristic of roots, not stems. Also, monocot bundles are closed, not open.

options.text: They are bicollateral, scattered, closed, and exarch.
options.explanation: Monocot bundles are collateral, not bicollateral (found in some dicot stems like Cucurbita), and xylem is endarch, not exarch.

questions.explanation: In a monocotyledonous stem, the vascular bundles are typically scattered in the ground tissue, unlike the ring arrangement seen in dicot stems. They are conjoint (xylem and phloem are on the same radius), collateral (xylem towards the inner side and phloem towards the outer side), and most importantly, closed (lacking a cambium between xylem and phloem, hence no secondary growth). The xylem is endarch, meaning protoxylem lies towards the pith and metaxylem towards the periphery.
questions.subject: neet-botany
